name: Atlanticism
summary: Atlanticism holds that North America and Europe should be bound by close political, economic and above all security ties, centred on NATO and a shared commitment to liberal democracy, individual liberty and the rule of law. It is chiefly a foreign-policy outlook, with Russia as the main threat historically and strategic competition from Russia and China in its modern 'New Atlanticism' form, and takes no firm line on most domestic questions.
scope: The mainstream postwar and contemporary transatlantic tradition as expressed in the Atlantic Charter (1941), the North Atlantic Treaty (1949) and NATO's 2022 Strategic Concept, including the 'New Atlanticism' revision. It excludes continentalist European projects that deliberately distance themselves from the US, and specific party platforms; because the doctrine is about alliance rather than domestic policy, most answers on economic and social questions are low-confidence inferences.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Atlanticism is a foreign-policy and security orientation with no healthcare doctrine; its adherents span the US center-left and the European right, so they split.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Wage policy is outside the doctrine, and adherents range across the US center-left and the European right.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The Atlantic Charter's points on equal trade access and the shared Western order lean market-liberal, but this is inferred rather than stated.

public-ownership.rationale: Postwar Atlantic institutions built a liberal market order; nationalisation is not part of the doctrine, inferred from that.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: No taxation doctrine; adherents are split between US center-left and European right.

unions-good.rationale: Not addressed; Atlanticists come from both labor-friendly and business-friendly traditions.

property-fundamental.rationale: The Treaty's preamble names individual liberty and the rule of law as the shared civilisation, which implies property protection but does not say so.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Outside the doctrine and split across its adherents.

cut-welfare.rationale: Charter point 5 endorses cooperation for improved labor standards and social security, so cutting welfare is not a doctrinal aim.

worker-ownership.rationale: Not part of the transatlantic liberal order; inferred from its market-liberal orientation.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Security cooperation is central but surveillance trade-offs divide adherents, as with rifts over US intelligence practices.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not addressed; transatlantic adherents differ as US and European law differ on speech.

strong-leader.rationale: The Treaty grounds the alliance in democracy and rule of law, which sits poorly with bypassing legislatures.

limit-guns.rationale: No doctrine; US and European adherents differ on guns.

empower-police-military.rationale: Article 3 commits members to maintain and develop their capacity to resist armed attack, which supports adequate military funding; police is inferred.

decide-locally.rationale: The doctrine favours supranational and alliance-level coordination, so localism is not emphasised; inferred.

traditional-family.rationale: Atlanticism is a values-of-liberal-democracy orientation without family doctrine; adherents split.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split across left and right.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; adherents split.

more-religion-public.rationale: The Treaty's civilisational bond is framed by democracy, liberty and rule of law, not religion; inferred.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Atlanticism stresses a shared Western civilisation across nations more than any single national culture; adherents mixed.

gradual-change.rationale: Atlanticism defends institutions created after 1945 such as NATO, so it leans toward institutional continuity; inferred.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not a doctrinal issue, but Atlanticism is an internationalist outlook with openness to transatlantic ties; inferred and contested.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The Treaty reaffirms the UN Charter and builds a permanent multilateral alliance, though Atlanticists prioritise NATO over the UN itself.

free-trade.rationale: Charter point 4 calls for equal access to trade and raw materials for all states, and Treaty Article 2 urges removing conflict in economic policies.

nation-first.rationale: The doctrine rests on mutual defence and collective cooperation, with Article 5 treating an attack on one as an attack on all.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: NATO's cooperative-security and crisis-management tasks permit this, but Atlanticism itself is a security-alliance doctrine, and Iraq divided adherents.

open-borders.rationale: Not a doctrinal aim; the focus is on alliance membership rather than borderless movement.

limit-growth.rationale: Charter point 5 favours improved economic advancement, inferred to oppose growth limits.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Climate has been added to NATO's agenda but is not core to Atlanticism; adherents split.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: The Strategic Concept stresses technological innovation to keep the alliance's edge, though not as a general doctrine.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Not addressed; nuclear power is not part of the doctrine.

revolution-justified.rationale: The Treaty is grounded in the rule of law and defence of the existing liberal order, which opposes revolution.

experts-over-public.rationale: The doctrine is associated with foreign-policy elites and think tanks but also with democratic values; split.

central-planning.rationale: The Atlantic Charter and the postwar Atlantic order endorse market access and free institutions, opposed to the Soviet model Atlanticism arose against.

socialized-markets.rationale: Inferred from the liberal market orientation of the Atlantic order.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Estate taxation is a domestic fiscal question the alliance doctrine never touches; adherents differ by party.

basic-income.rationale: Income support is a domestic welfare matter outside the security and trade focus of the doctrine.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Charter point 4 and Treaty Article 2 seek to reduce conflict in economic policies and open trade, though transatlantic trade disputes occur.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The Atlantic liberal order favours open economic cooperation over state direction; inferred.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Distribution of property ownership is not addressed in the Charter or Treaty, so adherents have no common view.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Wholly outside the liberal market order Atlanticism defends; inferred.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: No doctrine, but Atlanticism supports established institutions like the IMF and World Bank.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Not part of the doctrine; inferred from its liberal-democratic framing.

one-party-rule.rationale: The Treaty founds the alliance on democracy and individual liberty, in opposition to one-party states.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Atlanticism includes monarchies like the UK and Canada but has no view on the form of state.

democracy-best.rationale: The Treaty preamble names democracy as the foundation of the shared civilisation and Article 10 limits membership to states advancing its principles.

direct-votes.rationale: Treaty emphasis is on representative democracy and rule of law; inferred.

workers-councils.rationale: Contrary to the liberal democratic institutions the alliance upholds.

right-to-secede.rationale: Charter point 2 backs territorial change only by the freely expressed wish of peoples, but alliance practice favours existing borders; inferred.

natural-rulers.rationale: Inferred from the Treaty's commitment to democracy and individual liberty.

political-violence-never.rationale: Article 5 authorises armed force in collective defence, so adherents do not hold that force is never justified.

war-builds-character.rationale: Charter point 8 calls for abandoning force and freeing people from fear, and NATO is framed as defensive.

separate-church-state.rationale: The shared values are liberal democracy and the rule of law, with no religious basis; inferred.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The Treaty names rule of law and individual liberty, not scripture, as the basis of the shared civilisation.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Article 3 and 5 rest defence on state capacity and collective state action.

military-superiority.rationale: Article 3 commits members to maintain collective capacity to resist armed attack, and NATO documents stress a military edge, though framed as deterrence.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The alliance is built on shared values, not ethnicity, and spans many nations.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The Charter posits cooperation among nations, not class conflict, as the path to peace.

equal-outcomes.rationale: No doctrine; liberal-democratic framing emphasises rights over outcomes.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Indigenous land claims are not a transatlantic-alliance issue, and adherents in the US, Canada and Europe differ.

colonial-reparations.rationale: No doctrine; inferred from the establishment orientation of adherents.

civilizational-union.rationale: Atlanticism calls for close union across the North Atlantic on a basis of shared Western values and civilisational bond, though through alliance rather than political merger.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Atlanticism stresses shared obligations among allies but has no theory of personal ethics, so adherents split.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Environmental philosophy is outside the doctrine and adherents hold varied views.

limit-population.rationale: Population policy is not a concern of the Atlantic alliance and adherents have no shared position.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Charter point 5 and postwar Atlantic order aim at economic advancement, opposed to this view.

accelerate-technology.rationale: The Strategic Concept welcomes innovation but stresses managing risk; no doctrine on disruption.

human-enhancement.rationale: Bioethics of enhancement is not addressed by the doctrine and adherents are divided.

algorithmic-government.rationale: NATO's technology principles stress responsible use consistent with democratic values; inferred.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: No doctrine; security and liberty considerations split adherents.

restore-past-order.rationale: Atlanticism defends the existing postwar order rather than restoring a lost one.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Atlanticism is described as tied to political expedience, which suggests pragmatic outlook.

direct-action.rationale: Contrary to the Treaty's commitment to democratic institutions and rule of law.

means-match-ends.rationale: The doctrine is a diplomatic and military alliance posture, with no stated view on prefigurative methods.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Wholly opposed to the economic advancement sought in the Charter.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Opposed to the economic cooperation the doctrine supports; inferred.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Charter point 5 favours social security but not distribution by need as a principle; inferred.

production-for-use.rationale: Inferred from the market-liberal order the Charter envisions.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Contrary to the market-oriented liberal order Atlanticism defends.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Treaty rests on democracy, individual liberty and rule of law, in contrast to the Soviet-bloc systems NATO formed against.

collective-farming.rationale: Associated with the Soviet system opposed by Atlanticism.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: The Charter holds that open trade and cooperation promote peace.

taxation-theft.rationale: Not a doctrinal view; inferred as inconsistent with state-funded collective defence.

harm-principle.rationale: The Treaty values individual liberty but states no limit on state power in the Millian sense; adherents differ.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The Treaty stresses individual liberty but has no doctrine on group rights.

conscription.rationale: NATO members differ widely; no doctrine.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The Treaty prizes democratic institutions, so voting is not subordinated to exit.

state-as-business.rationale: No doctrine; inferred from democratic framing.

positive-liberty.rationale: Charter point 6 speaks of freedom from want and fear, but adherents split on the broader claim.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Charter and Treaty rest on equal peoples and shared liberal values; no racial hierarchy.

organic-representation.rationale: Inferred from commitment to party-based liberal democracy.

total-state.rationale: Treaty commits to individual liberty and free institutions.

national-rebirth.rationale: Atlanticism defends existing order, not radical rebirth.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Charter point 1 renounces territorial aggrandisement, and NATO is defined as defensive.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Contrary to the rule of law in the Treaty.

bound-labor.rationale: Contrary to individual liberty in the Treaty's preamble.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: No doctrine; inferred from the Enlightenment-liberal heritage.

universal-morality.rationale: The Treaty claims a shared civilisation founded on democracy and liberty, which implies universal principles, though inferred.

single-common-good.rationale: Atlanticism combines liberal pluralism with alliance solidarity and takes no stance on a unitary common good.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Diaspora return rights are a national question the alliance doctrine does not address.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language revival is a national cultural matter outside the doctrine, with no common adherent view.

workplace-democracy.rationale: No doctrine; inferred from market orientation.

school-vouchers.rationale: Education funding is a domestic matter, and adherents split along party lines in each country.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal stance is not part of the doctrine, and US and European adherents differ on stimulus.

economic-freedom.rationale: Charter point 4 and Article 2 link free institutions to economic cooperation, though not stated as a precondition.

rule-by-example.rationale: The Treaty stresses rule of law.

national-self-determination.rationale: Charter point 3 affirms the right of all peoples to choose their government, and sovereignty restoration for those deprived of it.

force-without-un.rationale: Atlanticists split: NATO acted without a Security Council mandate in Kosovo and Iraq divided adherents; Article 5 itself defers to the Security Council.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The Treaty's civilisation rests on liberty and law, not an epistemology; adherents include both religious and secular people.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Welfare eligibility is a domestic matter beyond the alliance doctrine, and adherents differ.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Workfare is a domestic policy dispute, not part of Atlanticism, and adherents are divided.

class-collaboration.rationale: Charter point 5 favours cooperation to improve labor standards; inferred.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Atlanticism values the shared Western cultural tradition.

dominated-front.rationale: Atlanticism is itself the Western alliance, so a front against the West is its opposite.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The Treaty values individual liberty; inferred.

ban-interest.rationale: Inconsistent with the liberal economic order; inferred.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Contrary to the individual liberty and rule of law in the Treaty preamble.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The doctrine treats liberal democratic states as legitimate guarantors of freedom.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: No doctrine; adherents split, and energy independence from Russia is a concern.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Integration policy is outside the doctrine and varies among adherents from Britain to Germany to Canada.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy claim unrelated to the doctrine and contrary to its mainstream establishment adherents.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral systems differ across NATO members, and the doctrine sets no preference.

national-mission.rationale: Charter point 1 renounces gains, but US adherents sometimes hold democracy-promotion views; split.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The doctrine does not address gender structure, and adherents split between left and right.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Atlanticism is associated with the establishment, inferred.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Contrary to individual liberty and rule of law.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Accountability for past abuses is not addressed by the doctrine; adherents are split, particularly on allied conduct in wars.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Charter point 5 supports social security and economic cooperation, beyond a minimal state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Contrary to the individual liberty in the Treaty.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The Treaty grounds the shared civilisation in individual liberty and rule of law, which implies equality before the law.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Not applicable; inferred opposition to the socialist premise.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: No doctrine; Atlanticism includes settler states such as the US and Canada.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Personal-law regimes are a national legal question the alliance doctrine does not address.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Contrary to the individual liberty named in the Treaty.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Outside the doctrine and inconsistent with its liberal framing.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: School religion practice differs across members, and the doctrine sets no rule.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Charter points 2 and 3 base territorial change and government on the freely expressed wishes of peoples.

trade-surplus.rationale: Charter point 4 favours open trade on equal terms, not mercantilism.

population-transfer.rationale: Charter point 2 rules out territorial changes against the wishes of the peoples concerned.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Atlanticists accept collective armed force in defence under Article 5, though initiation of force is generally opposed.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: The Charter stresses cooperation among peoples.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Adherents split; German and US practices differ.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: This republican theory of liberty is not part of Atlanticist texts, and adherents hold varied views.

separated-powers.rationale: Rule of law and democratic institutions in the Treaty imply checks and balances, though inferred.

vanguard-party.rationale: Contrary to the democratic principles on which the alliance rests.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Social priorities are not addressed in the doctrine, and adherents vary across the spectrum.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: A British housing policy that the doctrine never touches, with adherents split by party.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Industrial relations law is a domestic issue outside the alliance doctrine.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Charter's emphasis on trade and cooperation suggests institutional causes; inferred.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: No doctrine; alliance spans many nations; inferred.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Inferred from commitment to representative democracy.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The Treaty's rule of law commitment weighs against it.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Inferred from the market-liberal Atlantic order.

party-controls-media.rationale: Contrary to individual liberty and free institutions.

party-commands-army.rationale: Contrary to democratic civilian control; Treaty rests on democratic institutions.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Naturalisation rules are national matters with no common transatlantic position.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Party organisation is not addressed, and Atlanticists sit in many differently run parties.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Atlanticism is related to but distinct from European integration, and adherents are split between pro-EU and those who favour NATO over the EU.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is irrelevant to the alliance doctrine, which names no religious basis.

clerical-rule.rationale: Contrary to democracy and the rule of law in the Treaty.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: The doctrine rests on collective defence and loyalty among allied governments.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Inferred from the commitment to individual liberty.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Inferred from democratic and rule-of-law commitments.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall procedures are a domestic constitutional matter, and members vary widely.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Atlanticism is the defence of permanent alliance, with Article 5 mutual defence and forward troop presence.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Inconsistent with the liberal economic order; inferred.

people-in-arms.rationale: Article 3 builds defence on collective state capacity and alliance forces.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The doctrine has no view on rural versus urban life.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: No doctrine, although German reunification within NATO was supported.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Atlanticism is an elite policy tradition; inferred.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: The Treaty asserts a shared civilisation founded on democracy and liberty, which implies ranking of political systems; contested.

death-penalty.rationale: European adherents oppose and US adherents split, noted as friction in transatlantic relations; inferred majority view.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: School curricula are a domestic matter on which adherents split by party and country.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Content regulation is not addressed by the doctrine, and adherents split.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Citizenship rules differ among members and the doctrine sets none.

minority-language-support.rationale: Language policy is national, and the doctrine takes no stance.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Religious exemptions are handled differently by members and the doctrine is silent.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Millian social philosophy is not part of Atlanticist writings, though the liberty theme leans mildly toward it; adherents are split.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Atlanticism supports World Bank and IMF institutions; inferred.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Charter point 3 secures political self-rule without requiring economic transformation.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Constitutional-drafting procedure is a national matter that the doctrine does not address.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Contrary to the individual liberty and democracy the Treaty affirms.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Charter point 5 speaks of economic cooperation, but no explicit aid duty; split.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Atlanticism relies on US extended deterrence within NATO, though the UK and France keep their own forces; split among European adherents.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Head-of-state selection varies among allied democracies, and the doctrine sets none.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Atlanticism includes the IMF and World Bank economic institutions; inferred.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Territorial concessions in specific disputes are not addressed by the doctrine, and adherents differ by case.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Atlanticism has no theory of property, and adherents differ between liberal and social-market views.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Not addressed; adherents regarded the USSR as a threat regardless of label.

state-harmful.rationale: The Treaty builds a permanent state-based alliance on collective state defence and the rule of law, so Atlanticists reject the claim that the state is unnecessary.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Atlanticists favour strong defence against hostile states but within democratic constitutions, and reject socialist-state doctrine; inferred.

collective-defense.rationale: Article 5 of the North Atlantic Treaty makes collective defence the core commitment of the alliance.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Atlanticism has no environmental doctrine and its adherents split between US and European approaches to risk; inferred.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: The Atlantic Charter rejects territorial change against the freely expressed wishes of peoples, and NATO treats annexations such as Crimea as illegal.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The treaty's commitment to individual liberty implies religious freedom, so curbing religious bodies is disfavoured; inferred.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Not an Atlanticist question; adherents live under both presidential and monarchical systems.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: The Charter backs self-determination, while members divide on cases such as Kosovo and Catalonia; adherents split.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Atlanticists generally welcome autonomy arrangements and criticised the erosion of Hong Kong's promised autonomy; inferred.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The alliance is founded on democracy, liberty and the rule of law, which exclude a sacred ruler.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Tax policy is outside the doctrine and adherents range from the US center-left to the European right.

character-from-environment.rationale: Atlanticism is silent on human nature; adherents split.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The North Atlantic Treaty commits members to the rule of law, under which rulers are bound by law.

space-expansion.rationale: NATO treats space as an operational domain but not as a civilizational goal; adherents split.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Atlanticism commits to liberal democracy without prescribing a constitutional form; inferred.

leader-cult.rationale: Mass veneration of a leader contradicts the individual liberty and democracy in the alliance's founding values.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family law is outside the doctrine; adherents split.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Atlanticism is rooted in liberal democracy and rejects Marxist-Leninist doctrine, a stance defined by the Cold War alliance against the Soviet bloc.

land-redistribution.rationale: Atlanticism has no land-reform doctrine; its commitment to the rule of law and individual liberty implies protecting existing property, inferred from the Treaty's preamble.

refugee-return.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; Atlanticists are split between those stressing refugee rights and those stressing settled outcomes.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: The Atlantic Charter renounces territorial aggrandisement and territorial changes against the wishes of the peoples concerned, and NATO treats forcible border revision as the core threat.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: The Treaty commits members to individual liberty and the rule of law, and liberal Atlanticists reject punishing religious exit; stated indirectly.

women-must-cover.rationale: Compulsory covering contradicts the individual liberty the Treaty names as a shared value; no Atlanticist source endorses it.

common-currency.rationale: The Treaty's economic cooperation article and Western integration lean toward monetary union, but the doctrine is silent and the UK and US keep national currencies.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Atlanticism defends existing borders and a Western alliance of sovereign states; ethnic political unification is inferred to be foreign to it.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Minority cultural autonomy is not addressed; liberal adherents differ on integration versus autonomy.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Liberal rights within existing states fit the Atlantic Charter's liberal order, but the doctrine does not address minority emigration; inferred.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Atlanticism is a liberal tradition that gives weight to ideas and institutions such as the Charter's principles, though it has no theory of history; inferred.

ban-cartels.rationale: Open-market principles in the Atlantic Charter imply competition protection, but antitrust is not part of the doctrine.

no-bailouts.rationale: No bailout doctrine; the alliance's market-liberal leaning is offset by Western governments' record of rescues, so a mild disagree is inferred.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: The Treaty names the rule of law as a founding value alongside democracy, which implies courts constrain majorities.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Gender quotas are not addressed; adherents range across the US center-left and European right.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: The Atlantic Charter calls for equal access to trade and raw materials and for economic collaboration, the opposite of closed blocs.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Trade standards are outside the doctrine; the Charter stresses open trade and improved labour standards in the same text, so adherents split.

moral-incentives.rationale: Atlanticism is a liberal market-order tradition with no place for moral incentives replacing pay; inferred.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Atlanticism opposes revolutionary violence against democratic orders and renounces the use of force in the Charter.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Liberal democratic order is inconsistent with inherited rank, but the UK's Atlanticists keep monarchy and peerage, so the answer is a weak inference.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Atlanticism is a foreign-policy outlook with no curriculum doctrine; adherents are split.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The Atlantic Charter affirms the right of all peoples to choose their government, which runs against rule of other societies; the doctrine is not about colonial tutelage, so partly inferred.

patriotic-education.rationale: Not part of the doctrine; adherents range across the center-left and the right.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: A domestic issue outside the doctrine; adherents split.

public-money-creation.rationale: Not addressed; adherents are mainstream liberal-market internationalists who accept private-bank money creation; inferred.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Not addressed; the Western market-economy order the alliance defends assumes capitalism adapts; inferred.

former-empire-influence.rationale: NATO's 2022 Strategic Concept rejects spheres of influence and Russian claims over former imperial lands, a position Atlanticism treats as a threat.

delink-world-market.rationale: The Atlantic Charter calls for access to trade and raw materials on equal terms and Article 2 of the Treaty promotes economic collaboration, so delinking runs against it.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Not addressed; the transatlantic liberal order assumes shared interests among its peoples; inferred.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Not addressed; adherents largely accept liberal-democratic anti-discrimination law; inferred.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The North Atlantic Treaty commits members to individual liberty and the rule of law, which fits entrenched constitutional guarantees; the doctrine does not address bills of rights directly.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Not an Atlanticist issue; no position documented.

elective-rulers.rationale: Atlanticism rests on shared liberal democracy as a founding value, so elected rulers are inferred.

minority-veto.rationale: Inferred from democratic majority rule with rights; NATO itself uses consensus among states, but that is not the same issue.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Inferred from the rule of law and liberty stressed in the treaty and charter.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Inferred from the parliamentary democracies that make up the alliance.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Atlanticism has no position; mainstream Western opinion inferred.

animal-use-humane.rationale: No position; mainstream Western opinion inferred.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Atlanticism takes no firm line on domestic social questions.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Atlanticism stresses engagement and collective responsibility in foreign affairs; inferred.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Inferred from liberal pluralist outlook; class-hegemony analysis is not part of the tradition.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: The Atlantic Charter endorses access to trade and raw materials for all states and economic collaboration; dependency theory is inferred to be rejected.

party-own-road.rationale: The statement concerns communist parties; no Atlanticist position.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Atlanticism favours economic collaboration and investment among allies; inferred.

return-lost-territory.rationale: The Atlantic Charter opposed territorial changes against the freely expressed wishes of peoples, and the alliance upholds existing borders; inferred.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Inferred from the equal citizenship of liberal democracy.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: The Atlantic Charter looks to the destruction of Nazi tyranny; an anti-fascist constitutional value is inferred as compatible.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Atlanticism arose against both Nazism and Soviet communism; joint condemnation is inferred.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Atlanticism takes no line on this domestic issue.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Atlanticism takes no line on this domestic issue.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: The treaty and the 2022 Strategic Concept promote democracy and individual liberty as shared values; inferred to be treated as universal rather than civilisation-specific.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Inferred from democratic civilian control of the armed forces within the alliance.

paid-care-work.rationale: Atlanticism takes no line on this domestic issue.

filial-duty.rationale: The Treaty addresses alliance, not family duties; inferred as outside the doctrine, with adherents split.

office-by-exam.rationale: Inferred from the commitment to democratic institutions and the rule of law, which favours elected and accountable officials over examination rule.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: The Atlantic Charter favours open trade, but alliance members routinely screen strategic purchases; adherents are split.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Inferred from the liberal commitment to individual liberty in the North Atlantic Treaty; no document addresses divorce.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Inferred from the Treaty's representative democratic institutions; binding mandates and instant recall are not part of the tradition.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Not addressed; the tradition is silent on pension design and its member states differ widely.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Inferred from the Atlantic Charter's liberal economic order and open access to resources, which assumes private property in land.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Inferred from the Treaty's commitment to democratic institutions and the rule of law, which includes legislative control of the budget.

single-official-language.rationale: Inferred from liberal pluralism among the member states; the alliance has no language policy and most members are multilingual.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the Charter's open trade and economic cooperation among allies, which cuts against blanket bans on foreign buyers.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Not addressed; the 2022 Strategic Concept notes shared values but takes no line on race and discrimination law.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Inferred from the Atlantic Charter's goal of better living standards through open economic collaboration, which treats consumption as a good.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Not covered by the founding texts; members have backed rebels at times, and adherents are split between interventionists and critics.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: The Charter and Treaty stress self-determination, sovereignty and renouncing force, so no ally may coerce another by arms.

corporate-influence.rationale: Atlanticism is a foreign-policy outlook with no position on lobbying; inferred neutral.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: The 2022 Strategic Concept treats hybrid threats and foreign interference as security matters, so limits on hostile foreign funding fit; inferred.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: No Atlanticist position on population policy; inferred neutral.

residents-only-property.rationale: Atlanticism favours open liberal economies and shared Western property norms; inferred mild disagreement.

job-guarantee.rationale: Atlanticism's market-liberal economic orientation disfavours a state employer of last resort; inferred.

democratic-peace.rationale: Atlanticism is framed around shared liberal democracy, and defenders commonly link democratic spread with peace; inferred.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The North Atlantic Treaty commits members to the rule of law; inferred that adherents accept a general duty to obey.

non-intervention.rationale: Atlanticists accept collective intervention and common action by allied states, so an absolute ban on intervention is rejected.

industrial-unions.rationale: Atlanticism takes no position on union structure; inferred.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Atlanticism's liberal-democratic values reject ethnic conspiracy claims; inferred.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Atlanticism has no position on marriage law; inferred disagreement from its mainstream liberal-democratic orientation.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Open government is part of the liberal-democratic values Atlanticism upholds; inferred.

local-production.rationale: Atlanticism favours open transatlantic trade over local self-reliance; inferred.

informal-organisation.rationale: Atlanticism is built on formal institutions and treaties; inferred.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Atlanticism rests on treaty commitments and a rules-based order that members treat as binding, so national law overriding international obligations is rejected.

religious-nation.rationale: Atlanticism is a secular alliance of liberal democracies; inferred.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: The Atlantic Charter and the North Atlantic Treaty rest on sovereign equality and self-determination, not tribute or submission.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Atlanticism is silent on regional budgets and its adherents differ; inferred.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Atlanticism affirms individual liberty and market-friendly open trade, so it is inferred to oppose common ownership of the means of production.

defeat-communism.rationale: NATO was founded to deter and counter the Soviet Union, and the alliance has historically treated communist rule as a threat.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Public service delivery is outside the doctrine, and adherents span centre-left and centre-right; inferred.

religion-illusion.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from its liberal-democratic values, which defend freedom of belief and do not treat religion as an illusion.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Inferred from the Atlantic Charter's support for open trade and economic cooperation among liberal democracies.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from liberal-democratic values that favour law and attitudes over wholesale economic transformation.

socialized-care.rationale: Not addressed; domestic care policy is outside the doctrine, and its liberal values lean toward private arrangements.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from its liberal values and commitment to open exchange among allied nations.

treaties-binding.rationale: Inferred from the alliance's stress on the rule of law and honouring commitments.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Inferred from its liberal-democratic commitments to individual liberty and open trade, which do not fit communal property.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred from its stress on self-determination and rule of law, which cuts against state-steered settlement.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Atlanticism is anchored in liberal democracy and market economies and rejects both extremes; it does not seek a third course. Inferred.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Atlanticism is an alliance doctrine with no stance on historical land claims; adherents hold varied views. Inferred.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Its shared values of liberty and the rule of law sit with mainstream democratic tradition, which rejects denial; the doctrine itself never addresses it. Inferred from those values.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: The alliance rests on individual liberty and the rule of law, which point against criminalising private conduct, though it takes no line on the issue.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The North Atlantic Treaty commits members to democracy, individual liberty and the rule of law, which exclude suppressing opposition for order.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Individual liberty is a founding value of the Treaty, which is incompatible with state punishment of blasphemy. Inferred from that value.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The Atlantic Charter endorses self-determination and disclaims territorial aggrandisement, which cuts against governing colonies for the ruling country's benefit.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Atlanticism never addresses Islamic doctrine; its security outlook treats militant jihadism as a threat, so it would not endorse this as a duty. Inferred.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: The Treaty favours peaceful, constitutional politics and rule of law over forcible removal of governments, though it takes no line on religious law. Inferred.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Participatory democracy is outside the doctrine; adherents range from technocratic to participatory views. Inferred.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: A foreign-policy doctrine with no position on intersectionality; adherents split across the centre-left and the right.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Gender identity law is outside the doctrine and adherents span the US centre-left and the European right.

assisted-dying.rationale: Assisted dying is outside the doctrine; adherents divide, and transatlantic friction on bioethics is noted.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Atlanticism is a bipartisan consensus bridging left and right on security, but it does not claim the division is obsolete. Inferred.

alienated-labor.rationale: The doctrine has no theory of labour; its commitment to open trade and market economy implies it would not accept this critique. Inferred.

islam-incompatible.rationale: The alliance is founded on shared liberal values and treats its members as one community; it does not frame Islam as incompatible. Inferred.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The Treaty grounds the alliance in democracy and the rule of law, with authority resting on peoples and constitutions rather than God.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: State secularism is outside the doctrine and its member states differ on it.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: A domestic employment-law question the doctrine never addresses; adherents are split.

social-market-economy.rationale: The Treaty encourages economic collaboration and the Atlantic Charter open trade, fitting a regulated market economy; inferred.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The Treaty's core is collective defence by armed forces, and NATO's 2022 Strategic Concept reaffirms deterrence and defence as a core task.

rich-first.rationale: Development sequencing is outside the doctrine; adherents range across economic views.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Atlanticism is membership of and commitment to the Western military bloc, NATO, so staying out contradicts it.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Atlanticism rests on liberal democracy and individual liberty, which sit uneasily with hereditary rule; inferred, since the doctrine does not address succession.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Credit institutions are outside this foreign-policy doctrine, and adherents range from market liberals to social democrats.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Mainstream Atlanticists work through Western-led institutions and generally accept lender conditionality; inferred, not a stated doctrine.

property-franchise.rationale: The North Atlantic Treaty commits members to democracy and individual liberty, and the Atlantic Charter to government by consent, which cuts against wealth-based voting.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Ecofeminist theory is not addressed by the doctrine and adherents are split.

reification.rationale: Adherents come from the liberal-democratic mainstream, which does not take up the Marxist reification critique; inferred.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: The alliance's commitment to individual liberty implies treating press and assembly freedoms as real despite private ownership; inferred.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The North Atlantic Treaty preamble names the rule of law as a founding value, and NATO's 2022 Strategic Concept reaffirms it.

racial-franchise.rationale: The treaty's commitment to individual liberty and democracy, and the Charter's self-determination of peoples, are incompatible with racial limits on voting.

online-participation.rationale: The doctrine is silent on online participation and adherents are split; inferred.

open-government-data.rationale: Open, accountable government follows from the democratic values the alliance affirms; inferred.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Individual liberty and the rule of law imply no legal limits on interfaith marriage; inferred from the treaty's stated values.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Religious boycotts contradict the individual liberty and equal treatment the alliance affirms; inferred.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Atlanticism is an alliance and security doctrine with no position on deliberative democracy; adherents span parties that differ on it. Inferred from its commitment to liberal democracy generally, which does not settle the question.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Atlanticism has no doctrine on religion; it is a foreign-policy outlook, and adherents range from secular liberals to religious conservatives. Nothing in the sources addresses it.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Atlanticism is a security and foreign-policy outlook with no doctrine on wealth; adherents range across the spectrum.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the alliance's commitment to individual liberty, and most member states permit open service.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The North Atlantic Treaty commits members to individual liberty; state promotion of atheism is inferred to conflict with that.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from adherents' mainstream liberal-democratic, rule-of-law outlook.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Not addressed; adherents hold varied views on domestic constitutional design.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Domestic social policy is outside the doctrine and adherents split between center-left and center-right.

term-limits.rationale: Not addressed; domestic institutional design is outside the doctrine.

vote-delegation.rationale: Inferred from the alliance's commitment to representative liberal democracy; delegable direct voting is not part of it.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; NATO's strategic concept focuses on state threats rather than extinction risk.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from its liberal-democratic principles of individual liberty.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from its liberal-democratic principles of individual liberty and equality before the law.

missingStatements.text: An armed attack on one allied country should be treated as an attack on all of them.
missingStatements.rationale: Article 5 of the North Atlantic Treaty makes collective defence the core commitment of the alliance.

missingStatements.text: Democratic countries should be admitted to a permanent military alliance if they share its values and can contribute to its security.
missingStatements.rationale: Article 10 permits invitation of European states that advance the treaty's principles, and NATO's 2022 invitation to Finland and Sweden reaffirmed this.
missingStatements.declined: Narrow to NATO membership procedure; an alliance-specific detail rather than a broad position.

notes: Atlanticism is strongest in the UK, Eastern and Central Europe and Poland, weaker among supporters of a strong EU such as in Germany and France. The Iraq War and Trump-era disputes divided adherents on unilateral force and burden-sharing.
